answer: Duty, not fees, can price out sybils. Each epoch, 10% of identities are conscripted by lottery to verify random peers; refusal forfeits the epoch's payout from the vault of copper credits. The pool is fixed, so per-identity reward decays as 1/N while duty stays constant. An operator running k fakes collects k/N of the pool yet owes 0.1k random checks, so collusion cannot self-assign the lottery. Once 100/N copper credits drops below one verification's cost, every extra identity is net negative; the fable that identity is free ends where marginal reward meets marginal duty.
